ist_001: You can recognise it by its immense hollow trunk, 4.5 metres across, fed only by a thin surviving layer of outer bark. It stands inside the university forestry research station in Bahçeköy's Belgrad Forest.
ist_002: You can recognise it by its low, spreading limbs that touch the ground and thicken into what look like separate trunks, the Octopus shape. It stands at a bend on the old Çayırbaşı to Bahçeköy road.
ist_003: You can recognise it by the second-hand booksellers' stalls set up beneath its canopy every day. It stands at the entrance to the Sahaflar Çarşısı book bazaar on Beyazıt Meydanı.
ist_004: You can recognise it by the visible cavity partway up its trunk, left after a centuries-old embedded stone was removed. It stands on Alemdar Caddesi outside Gülhane Park's Alemdar gate.
ist_005: You can recognise it by its uneven, still-recovering crown, propped upright after a 2017 storm tore it from the ground. It stands at Çengelköy's ferry pier square beside the Çınaraltı tea garden.
ist_006: You can recognise them by their tall, dark, narrow cypress columns rising above the gravestones around them. They stand scattered through Karacaahmet Mezarlığı, Turkey's largest cemetery, in Üsküdar.
ist_007: You can recognise it by its broad stone pine crown reaching 25 metres, among a grove of younger, individually named pines. It stands in Küçük Çamlıca Korusu, the hilltop park these pines gave its name.
ist_009: You can recognise it by its tall, narrow, pyramid-shaped cypress form, about 18 metres high on an ordinary residential street. It stands on Şehit Murat Yüksel Sokak on the car-free island of Büyükada.
ist_010: You can recognise them by the small group of broad old planes standing apart across an open meadow, the Bosphorus visible beyond. They stand on Beykoz Çayırı, the former Sultan's hunting meadow.
ist_012: You can recognise it by its tall, straight trunk about 170 centimetres across, rising to 33 metres. It stands in Gülhane Park, about 40 metres from the registered nettle tree beside it.
ist_013: You can recognise it as the hackberry rather than a plane, a slimmer trunk about 145 centimetres across and 23 metres tall. It stands in Gülhane Park, about 40 metres from the registered London plane.
ist_014: You can recognise it by its dark, dense, modest yew crown, only 13 metres tall beside the taller planes elsewhere on this list. It stands in Topkapı Palace's Fourth Courtyard, near the Baghdad Kiosk.
